- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior day), model should not overcorrect — cap forecast rise to 3–5% per day to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model should not ignore the event weight — reduce forecast slope by 1–2% per event.  
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.00) and price is rising, model should reverse trend early — reduce forecast slope by 1–3% to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model should not hold flat — adjust downward 1–2% per day to reflect reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 15-day moving average, model should adjust forecast to align with recent 15-day trend, not 30-day baseline.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67) and events are frequent, model should not assume neutrality — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to account for event-driven volatility.
